answer: Harness-fingerprint attestation binds each identity to a signed runtime bundle—process tree, syscall cadence—hashed with a tundra-seeded boot value and orchard-salted registry; peers swap partial hashes via a whisper channel. Joining costs a per-attempt bond, three independent attesters, and seventy-two hours before voting weight. An operator splitting identities pays that bond and latency each time; a coordinated ring fails because shared harness traits merge its apparent independence into one detectable cluster.
